notes.title: Devlog #5: Alpha and More!
notes.content:
Welcome to devlog #5! We're finally at the point where alpha testing is right around the corner!

Character Reveal: Grayson Brannigan

Before we start the overview, we've got a couple more characters to fully reveal. These characters have been present in previous promotional materials, but we haven't gotten the chance to get to know them yet. Running up the back line is Grayson Brannigan! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/717d3e2714009d94aa2382e62081361c32b0be88.png

Grayson takes on a friendly, older brother-like role in the story. He's sociable, easy-going, and is genuinely committed to helping out his comrades. While most of the members of the squad are present out of obligation, Grayson's here on his own accord. His ultimate goal is to reclaim his hometown from Egdel—but are his motives pure, or driven by revenge?

Grayson brings a new spin on ranged attackers by utilizing guns in combat. Guns have a range of 2-5 nodes away, more than bows' 2-3 range. However, they can only fire in cardinal directions. You'll need to position Grayson well in order to make the most of his restrictions, but doing so offers powerful damage from a safer distance.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/c272f9a2cc979f1816e9f88af57fb796eea83573.png

Grayson takes sniping to the extreme with his Inner Vision, Deadeye. After activation, Grayson can increase his already massive attack range for the rest of the turn. When used correctly, he can fire upon enemies who have no hope of reaching him. Do keep in mind his limited mobility, as he tends to have less Stamina than the rest of the cast.

Character Reveal: Grover

And another one! After Grayson comes his trusty companion, Grover!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/99c04fd8154419dd10b597c47009b2cb97026be8.png

Grayson found Grover during the Mad War all those years ago. Since then, the two have become inseparable. Grover has all the lovable traits of a dog—friendliness, playfulness, loyalty, the list goes on. He's as much of a fearsome presence on the battlefield as he is a calming one off of it. Where exactly he came from isn't known, as his previous owner seems to have vanished.

Grover's gameplay is fast-paced and wild, just like him. With a large Stamina pool, he can travel far and attack many times in one turn. Grover also wields a knife during combat, which can attack from close or far range. No other weapon type allows this, so Grover is best used by weaving him in and out of enemy lines to minimize his own risks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/2cd212886c062f2433affad69e4368bc88f18324.png

Several of his skills are concerned with movement and positioning. For example, he learns the Highwayman Command, which swaps the position of himself and the enemy after a clash. It's powerful to move enemies around, but do be careful not to overextend Grover, as he is quite frail.

And with that, we've revealed the new playable characters that will be playable during the Arc 1 alpha and betas! Do note that this is only a portion of the full roster, with the rest of them being made playable in future builds! Even with the current roster, you'll still be able to choose different team compositions over multiple playthroughs, further magnified by features like the Comrade Duo system and other mechanics. Having a great variety of choices is a core aspect of the game, and it's only going to get better!

Maps are Getting a Makeover!

One opportunity that running the Kickstarter gave us was the ability to get feedback from completely new people! So, we were taking notes on how people liked or disliked certain aspects of the game—with one important sticking point being presentation of the maps.

Previously, Stratagem Lost used 32x32 sprites to represent characters on the map. Pixelated graphics are a style that's rather common for many SRPGs, and it's easy to see why. It prioritizes readability, making it so that each character is distinct and easily recognized from a glance. Even games that feature fully 3D models in battle animations sometimes use them, as it's important for players to know exactly who each character is on the map.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/19817e313aa9fbbe329607f57ea27eabc84c8e89.png

However, for some people, this style felt weak and disjointed, especially compared to the battle animations being detailed and bombastic. Truthfully, this arises from the map sprites being some of the oldest assets in the game—long before battle animations were first conceptualized.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/44104ed6259a8104fcd54779fbcdac646cdf7d2e.png

This image is from 2019. The game's presentation and overall atmosphere has greatly developed since then. In general, sophistication and fidelity have been improved on.

With that, we took player feedback into account and decided to take another look at the map presentation. There were several different approaches we had, but eventually we decided to upscale the sprites while keeping the general silhouettes to preserve readability.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/571445246dc83cfd2dca33d2334491dc696952ee.png

There is a noticeable change in style that comes with it—the sprites are more detailed, even allowing Stratagem Lost's line texturing that the battle animations and visual novel portraits have. We believe that the main benefit is keeping the game's presentation consistent with itself, as now the gap between battle sprites and map sprites has been lessened.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/c999c20b767daeeda0322798f9556cc7ff241a1c.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/ccc11f6c70a234ed3587d394e7d50a84e2d9d773.png

We'll still be gathering information on how people respond to the updated presentation. For those that prefer the old style, the alpha and beta builds for Arc 1 will include a "Retro Sprites" toggle to keep the sprites that were used in the Kickstarter demo. We are open to continuing support for retro sprites—even for future characters—if there's a demand for it. However, our current plan is that the current style will be the game's default style going forward.

Alpha Testing for Arc 1 Begins Soon!

We're happy to announce that we're starting alpha testing for the Arc 1 build shortly! We're covering this over on our Kickstarter page for those who are eligible for it! What this also means is that the beta for Arc 1 is soon to arrive as well!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/605216f38e5ed63c8107cf495538d12fb920daa4.png

And with that, we've covered everything that we needed to cover before testing starts later this month! As always, feel free to contact us for any questions or concerns you have! We appreciate your support in helping us reach this point, and we're happy to take this next step for the game!

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: Devlog #4: The Audio Update!
notes.content:
Welcome to devlog #4! This one is mainly focusing on audio! Alongside getting the game fully functional, we've been in the trenches getting the game's voice acting and audio ready for Arc 1's release. We'd like to preview some of the sounds you'll hear in the game!

Character Reveal: Harriet Colbourne

But before we jump into covering the audio, holding down the front line—it's Harriet Colbourne!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/bb8cdfa07de98eba1c534ebfe8e031e5b907a9d2.png
Harriet is about as rigid as it gets. She's stoic, tough, and utterly devoted to Anyta's future. To her, protecting Anyta is a mission, one where failure would be worse than death. It's debatable whether or not Harriet is even capable of relaxing—no one has seen her laugh before. However, sometimes her words carry less bravado than usual. It appears that not even the most durable suit of armor can shield the heart.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/d6bb951a6a593349d6e6f77873f44f31feb55a07.png

On the battlefield, Harriet serves as the premier tank in the roster. With strong bulk, further enhanced by blades, Harriet can take a lot of punishment. Her job is to maintain the enemy's attention and keep herself alive. To that end, she uses the Death Threat Command, which guarantees that the enemy will attack Harriet. Do note that Death Threat actually raises the enemy's offenses unless a Positive Mark is burned—use it with caution.

She eventually learns some other skills to help control enemies and protect allies. The game has its fair share of units devoted to defense, but no one else is committed to the role as much as Harriet.

Iterating the Sound

In preparation for future builds, we have went back in and revisited what the game sounds like. The Kickstarter demo utilized a lot of harsh, mechanical sounds for the game's UI, a remnant of earlier builds. 

Certain sounds have been swapped out for more bouncy, energetic sounds, like record scratching, and in general we're approaching the audio experience of the game with a lot more intentionality this time.

A notable addition is that the game now has an announcer. Certain games use an announcer or narrator to enhance the feeling of playing it, and we're following suit with a booming, suave voice. He'll present characters, give encouragement, and commentate on other parts of the game as you play through it.

Here's a small preview of what the announcer sounds like! Just know there's a lot more examples that you'll hear in game!

[previewyoutube=uXVRxr47ubk;full][/previewyoutube]

Music Preview!

Our composer, dante, has been hard at work developing new music tracks for the game! Here's a preview of one of the story tracks that the game will have — used for calmer moments in the narrative.

[previewyoutube=hPFaFaVDVko;full][/previewyoutube]

We're very proud of how the soundtrack's developing! There's much more to come in future builds and updates!

Voice Acting Preview!

As of now, we're wrapping up voice acting sessions for Arc 1's release! In total, we estimate that we've recorded over 1500+ lines amongst the current cast. And there's more to come in the future!

We wanted to include a small preview of the results, showcasing a couple characters whose performances have yet to be shown off in their entirety so far!

Do note that the audio is not yet finalized. Aspects like volume, filters, etc. may vary from this preview and the final product.

[previewyoutube=Ap9KfaO4YsM;full][/previewyoutube]

The Arc 1 build is planned to have a significant portion of the voice acting finished. Playable characters and enemies will be voiced, with some minor exceptions that will be sorted out in future builds.

Alpha Testing is Approaching!

Voice acting was the last major addition to be included in the game before we start the alpha testing, so know that we're quickly approaching that milestone. In the meantime, we're getting some of the last features ready and making sure everything is where it needs to be.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/b08a1608431652f323e32933837c3263c7d3bb0f.png

We'll be announcing the date that we start alpha testing as well as giving directions to backers on how to access it at a later date. The next devlog will most likely focus on giving an overview of what alpha testing will be like. Tentatively, you can expect alpha testing to start in about 2 months.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/febba7064f673b2855488e9af2def3a472563482.jpg

As always, thanks for reading the devlog! Big things are coming, so I hope to see you again for the next update!

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: Devlog #3: New Recruits!
notes.content:
Welcome to devlog #3! The game is steadily making progress, though certain things need a bit more time before we show them off. However, we're still hard at work on the game, and we'd like to show some of the upcoming features as we get closer to Arc 1!
 
Character Reveal: Kingsley Armstrong

Here comes a new fighter! Kingsley Armstrong is here to fight, improve, and then repeat!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/61dc28016204e8eaa9cb54f170bc73488255c806.png
Kingsley's a simple man with a simple life, being content in the everyday so long as he pursues his true passion—combat. To him, every fight is a story, with a lesson to be learned. He sees his place in the squad as an opportunity to battle new opponents and gradually better himself through his art. Between skirmishes, Kingsley is a friendly, approachable guy—not a drop of ill intent in his soul.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/5dbbf958973e7e66c195d4e69fe1965a2a0a1933.png

In combat, Kingsley excels in the front line, dealing high damage while being able to take a hit or two. The brawler gets some tools to build Aggro quicker than others, allowing him to take the pressure off of your squishier allies. One of his standout skills is the Seismic Force Passive. This makes Kingsley's attacks shove enemies back after combat, which can be used for offensive and defensive purposes. It also stacks with other knockback skills, including the universal Throw Command, turning minor displacements into massive journeys.

Professional Mercenary Reveal: Lance Viridis

We've got another Professional Mercenary heading your way—get ready for Lance Viridis!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/ae6df51796169f23d5352ffdc102e36fb3378a4e.png
Lance brings a lot to the team, even by just being present. Defense is his specialty, and being able to trigger Taunt allows him to take the pressure of of his allies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/53adbc04af40ca4d369dbd9d1d2368cc2b816553.png

Despite being a rookie, Lance is prepared to learn, and learn quickly. However, war does change a man over time—perhaps it'll change him as well.

Community Created Mercenary Results!

Thanks to everyone who participated in our Majority Duels event! It was really enjoyable to see the group come together to decide on a character, and we have our winner!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/9d26de409c0d420642aa8014a99cf666be8bd74e.png

 "The Plague" will be sure to make an appearance in Stratagem Lost's future builds! We can't say quite when it'll happen just yet, but we're going to make something truly unique based off this prompt!

Roster Menu Preview

Recently, a lot of work has gone into creating some of the game's progression systems and adding the appropriate graphics for them. We thought we'd give a preview of it, since players are going to be using these systems quite a bit in their playthroughs.

Here's your first look at the game's Roster Menu! You'll be using this for managing your squad, hiring mercenaries, getting new equipment, the list goes on! Pretty much all of your micro-managing and teambuilding are going to use this as a jumping off point!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/e02b73502ce1fff1c4d4528ddda4f9db7a3e05ed.png

The left tab is going to get a lot busier as more characters become available, as you might expect. Small detail—the background has a little bit of parallaxing that responds to your mouse movement!

A design ethos that has been present from the beginning has been giving the player a multitude of options, which extends to the game's equipment system. You can have Howden keep using his starting lance, or swap to a new one that prioritizes a different strategy like range, stat buffs, etc. There is no right or wrong answer, but there are a lot of choices. We'll be showing more of this in the future, as well as collecting information about backer created equipment—some of which we hope to include in Arc 1!

We had our Casting Call!

Since the last update, we've conducted our first public casting call for the characters in Stratagem Lost! We had over 4000+ total auditions!

We've already found an excellent list of voice actors for several characters that you'll see in Arc 1, as well as future characters! Look forward to seeing some incredible performances in the game!

What's Next?

Arc 1's alpha/beta testing is drawing closer! I'm happy to say that we're beginning to progress from isolated asset development to now connect the dots to form the full experience! We can't put an exact date on things yet, but we'll let you know! At some point, we're hoping to properly set expectations as far as what the alpha/beta builds will contain, and how backers will be able to access them.

Thanks for reading the devlog! Hope to see you again soon!

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: Devlog #2: New Faces!
notes.content:
Welcome to devlog #2! Hope everyone had a great winter holiday! Today, we're showing some new characters!
 
Character Reveal: Margo Rheedus

Here's a new character that we're formally revealing—Margo Rheedus! She's briefly appeared in some of the trailers and promos, but this is the first time we've talked about her.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/deabacc18ead4d4f01f2d03846e883c51fdfa6e9.png

Despite being drafted like the others, Margo's someone that belongs anywhere other than a battlefield. She's not exactly an intimidating person—anyone can see that just by looking at her. However, she's resigned to giving up on her own ambitions in order to support her family. While combat stresses her out, you won't see her express it much—she's not really that talkative.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/3172455820e5bac54876bafda05966de58a8c0e3.png

In combat, Margo brings a lot of support tools to the table. Wielding a bow, she's naturally able to out-range melee enemies. Her starting Command is Siphon Shot, which inflicts the Siphon status condition. Units will heal themselves when attacking those with Siphon. Combined with other skills that weaken enemies, Margo helps to keep the party alive and give them an advantage in combat.

We're planning to reveal some more of the characters that show up as the game is being developed! Before Arc 1's beta release, look forward to seeing some of the other units you'll be able to deploy!

Professional Mercenary Reveal: Akane Hakurei

We're happy to reveal the first new Professional Mercenary that'll be available to recruit—Akane Hakurei! She is the game's first mercenary created by a backer, and there's more to come in the future. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/465b2f7951f34db97faa2f1e8061fd06a8030d57.png

In combat, Akane helps units get more out of their critical hits, making them easier to land and making them give more Vision in order to get Positive Marks faster. Using her Command still requires Stamina, so players will have to be smart about getting the immediate and future benefits of it.

Backers can still pledge to create Professional Mercenaries like this—we haven't quite closed that opportunity yet. You can message us on Kickstarter for inquiries.

Other News
Over on our Kickstarter, we're starting Majority Duels, an event where the community creates a character that will be made into a Pro Mercenary in the full game.{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/eb57186672d22928d875b15b1217d54b0de9a573.png

Other than that, we're continuing to work on the game for Arc 1's release later this year!

Thanks for checking out the devlog! Big things are coming, so hang tight! Hope to see you again in the future!

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: DEVLOG #1: Events and Our Future!
notes.content:
Here's devlog #1! This one's pretty varied, and there's also some other announcements thrown in, but allow us to shed some light on current developments!

Our Tentative Schedule!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/b87bb86065742fc463b9fbf19b6ce54c21ab30f6.png

Here's probably the most important announcement on the list! This is our planned schedule as of right now. These are tentative dates, not set in stone by any means, but with how development is going, this looks like when it's all going to happen.

What this means for Arc 1 is that it's going to be finishing development around Q2 2025. Alpha builds will start 1-2 months before the beta is properly released for all backers.

Mechanic Spotlight: Aggro (Reworked)

During some devlogs, we'll be highlighting some of the game's mechanics and going over any changes that have been made from the demo. We're choosing to talk about Aggro first, since it's received the biggest rework since the demo's release.

Aggro was a mechanic that was already planned to get a rework before the demo, but the input players had from the demo further confirmed that it needed some rethinking.

First off, what does Aggro even accomplish? The demo's first chapters didn't mention Aggro much, since it's a subtler mechanic compared to movement, attacking, etc. However, it's quite important since it dictates which one of your units get attacked.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/0eab44aa547de0a60b1c4078af24a047b0ab72dd.jpg

Aggro determines which unit enemies decide to attack. In very early builds of the game, before it was even revealed, it was clear that enemies had a greater attack range than most other SRPGs. It was easy for enemies to dart across the map and pick off your weaker units, which felt frustrating. Aggro was the solution to this problem, as a method to direct enemy attacks gave the player more control over who was getting attacked.

However, Aggro was originally designed around each unit having an Aggro number, and a clunky Aggro percentage. It ended up not presenting as much control as desired, since the numbers were obfuscated behind a system that didn't convey well. It also meant that the player had to keep checking the Unit Bio, since calculating Aggro percentages required a lot of mental math.

Now, Aggro has been consolidated into a singular resource—no need for percentages. It's also no longer dependent on damage dealt, making Aggro easier to be planned around. Critical Amplification (damage boost when landing a critical hit) has also changed, since it was based on the unit's Aggro. It follows a similar design philosophy, now simply adding damage based on Aggro rather than using a complicated multiplication formula.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/2026524e3734a8518b5c82044c1fe33be010bb88.png

Aggro is lost when getting hit during the player phase, leading to a much more interesting swing of things, where Aggro is a resource that is constantly changing. Your units end up essentially playing hot potato, and it's much harder for one unit to handle defense entirely. We're much more satisfied with the mechanic, and we're excited to see how these changes influence the game going forward.

There are other changes to the game that will be showing up in the first alpha/beta releases, and we'll be continuing to update backers about that in the future! Based on feedback and testing from the demo, some of the other changes that we're planning to make in the future include:


Status effect changes
Throws and collision changes
UI changes/additions
Balance/scaling changes


Until Next Time!

Thanks for checking out the devlog! We're working on making the game as spectacular as we can, so hang tight! Hope to see you again in the future!

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: Demo Patch Notes 0.4.0.2 (10/28/24)
notes.content:
Thanks for playing Stratagem Lost! We've taken some of the feedback and errors that people have found and implemented solutions! There are some issues that are still being worked on.

0.4.0.2

Fixes/Additions

Adjusted auto toggle in novel segments. Auto should not skip or hang for too long on certain voiced lines.
Some grammar/typo fixes.
Prevented some crashes from lower end users due to shaders being compiled incorrectly.
Fixed a bug in which Hazel's Vanish {B} would make enemies unable to be targeted.


Known Issues

The game might slow down for some lower end players on the Battle Forecast when trying to initiate combat with Hazel or against the boss in Chapter 1, or against the boss in the Challenge Map. They are using color paletted code, which may be touched up in the future for performance reasons. 
If you're starting the game with a controller plugged in, Steam may or may not receive inputs correctly. Unplugging and replugging the controller may fix this. If it continues, playing the Itch version may fix this.
Opening the glossary on the end path menu while opening another menu might cause a crash.


If you encounter a crash, you can screenshot the error popup and send it to us at support@hybridfiction.com, or show it to us in our official community Discord.

Also, if you've enjoyed the demo, consider backing our Kickstarter!

Hey everyone,

Big day today! We're officially launching Stratagem Lost's demo to the public, and beginning its Kickstarter campaign!

The Kickstarter Begins!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/1d2fe661b4ebc2b3a5af33f4ba56538526e48e67.png

Another thing, we've released an extended trailer for the demo's launch! A couple of things are different compared to the announcement trailer—maybe there's even a couple of secrets in it?
[previewyoutube=Ir5jfWElBNM;full][/previewyoutube]

The Demo and Next Fest
The demo is out! Hopefully, some of you reading this found the game via Steam Next Fest! There's two playable chapters in the build, be sure to give it a shot!

Also, the game includes an optional challenge map! The results screen will display things like how many enemies you defeated, how many units you lost, and the difficulty you played on. Quick aside—the demo is currently the most definitive experience of the game, but there are some adjustments planned for the future. Certain mechanics will be overhauled, for instance.

The Aggro system is planned to be changed from a percentage into a token system, making it easier and more cohesive to determine who will be attacked.
Weapons that have higher/lower Strike costs than the norm like Rapiers and Blades will be slightly overhauled to account for the Comrade Duo system allowing inheritable Commands in later builds.

Thank you for your time,

notes.title: Kickstarter Campaign First Look
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We're a week away from the start of Stratagem Lost's Kickstarter campaign! This is going to be a sneak peak of the campaign that begins on 10/14/24—we can't reveal everything yet, but we'd like to talk briefly about some parts of it.

Professional Mercenaries
The Kickstarter campaign is going to include some common backer rewards like the game, soundtrack, artbook, etc. However, there are going to be a lot of creative rewards! One of the most interesting ones is getting to make your own Professional Mercenaries—these are assistants you can hire to bolster your units. They will be fully unique, with custom animations, visual designs, voice acting, and skills—all of which will be influenced by backers.

To give a small window into the process, let's take a look at one of Professional Mercenaries that has already been put into the game—Archbishop Magdalene.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/b8e99550c1f3ee4e72fe839b981d4b5af490db61.png
Magdalene is essentially the game's poster child for Professional Mercenaries. She actually originated from a manga I made in college. Though she was only on two pages, I loved her concept so much that I didn't want to leave her behind.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/3d34da4e560ca9c670932ec8785d113c4215317f.png
In the transition to Stratagem Lost, she became considerably larger. Primal fear is synonymous with her—a giant build feels natural. Her design and colors also changed, but she still has the same brutal, savage authority. We're encouraging creativity with Professional Mercenaries, so don't feel afraid to make some truly bizarre characters. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/0a1d2db6b4686e98d071677c5bb350aae3cac756.png
One of these characters is a Professional Mercenary. See if you can guess which one it is.

In addition, there are going to be some other options for backers, like designing enemies, NPCs, and equipment sets. There will be some more information about these at the campaign's launch!


Development Builds
We've mentioned players being able to try the game ahead of time in the past. What we're opting to do is to allow backers to play pre-release builds! We're wanting to release the game in chunks for backers, with each chunk containing new units, more story content, etc. Players can simply wait for the full game to be finished, but backers will be able to play it in advance and give feedback to improve the game.

A common trend with this campaign is placing emphasis on community feedback and involvement. This is a game that benefits heavily from communication between the developers and players. Once the campaign starts, we're going to be making announcements primarily on both Steam and our Kickstarter page. We'll also be making some fun little asides here and there like character showcases on our social medias!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/750ef940480f709138fc0d5f9b7233fe9143d080.png
Side note, we're going to have fun little goodies in the campaign too, like stickers! This one is my favorite—it really captures the character's personality.

As always, please do not hesitate to reach out to us on our Discord, Twitter, Instagram, or Facebook. We hope too see you at our Kickstarter's launch! Remember—it's a week from now, on the 14th!

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: Kickstarter Campaign Announcement!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

We have a major announcement to make—we're going to be holding a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign to fund the game's development!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/1d2fe661b4ebc2b3a5af33f4ba56538526e48e67.png

We’ve opened up a pre-launch page for the game’s Kickstarter campaign that starts October 14th, 2024! Follow the Kickstarter for updates—this will also allow us to reach more people!

Why Kickstarter?
Crowdfunding was decided upon for one main reason: freedom. Stratagem Lost's core identity is rooted in unbound expression. We wanted to make the game without giving up control or rights to external entities in exchange for funding.

However, the reality is that game development is expensive and time-consuming. In order to put our full focus on the game, we're choosing to crowdfund it so that we can safely build the game on our own terms. This route has been pivotal in the success of many indie games, which has allowed developers to craft experiences they wouldn't be able to otherwise.

What does this mean for the players?

Lowered Price: We're going to be able to sell the game for less! Being crowdfunded means that we’re able to make the game more accessible since we’re not focused on maximizing profits.
Backer Creativity: Dedicated backers will be able to craft certain parts of the game, like designing characters and equipment/skills! Probably the biggest attraction are Professional Mercenaries, which are completely custom characters that can bolster units in combat. We’re encouraging creativity, no matter how outlandish it may be!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/40426b31fba5683c0adc37054bca526aef3b2fd1.png
In-Progress Builds: Backers will be able to play builds of the game ahead of its release! In order to make the game the best it can be, we’ll be taking feedback as the game is made.


Making a Kickstarter is ultimately asking for a lot of trust, which we firmly understand. It's been mentioned before, but the demo coming October 14th, 2024 will provide a small slice of the game before you support us. Everything that we'll be proposing is within scope and all of the mechanics are already functional within the game's code.

For those that have questions, in addition to leaving a comment, please do not hesitate to open a dialogue with us on our Discord, Twitter, Instagram, or Facebook. Please understand that we may be slower to answer since we're currently recovering from Hurriance Helene and have limited access to power and internet, but we'll try to communicate as best as we can.

Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games

notes.title: DEVLOG #0: Road to the Demo
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

This is our first devlog! We're going to share some updates on development and give a preview of what we have planned in the future!

Thank You for the Support!
First off, thank you to everyone who's supported us on our social medias and Steam! We counted 300+ wishlists on Steam after about just 4 days! For an unannounced launch, that's excellent, we're really appreciative of the support!

We've also taken note of some feedback that we've received, and are working to improve certain parts of the game. Some art assets like maps did not meet the standards set by the rest of the game's art direction, so we've taken the time to touch up and even completely redraw some visuals that needed attention.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/dd4b12f5b53031272f25fc07b2d1a9445d51f613.png

Originally, a lot of maps were crafted with a more geometric style to communicate the level design clearly. However, as the game evolved, maps begun to have a looser, sketchy look to them. The story will take the characters on a large variety of locations, so each map is hand-drawn as opposed to using premade tiles. Clarity is still a priority, but maps are looking more in tune with the game's aesthetics!

The Game Plan
Like has been stated before, we're on track for a demo release on October 14th, 2024. However, we're also planning another announcement to be made by the end of this current month September, which will be related to the demo's release.

For those wondering what the demo will contain, it's going to have about 30-60 minutes of gameplay and story, across the game's first two chapters. This will be meant to give a brief slice of the game's experience, without going in too deep yet.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/e0c1685efd75d13eeca8b965953e48f0e1d66dca.png

However, work is being put towards an optional challenge map to be played after the story. This is for players who want to sink their teeth into Stratagem Lost's gameplay loop. You'll also be able to play as some characters who don't show up in the demo's story!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45163789/c12a25fd74897d4b55dd1fc8fce5359eb2564b23.png

We're also not doing much hand-holding for this map — you'll simply be dropped into the map and left to fend for yourself! This is a challenge, focused on survival. Being able to get through the whole encounter without losing any units is an impressive feat, so we think advanced players will appreciate having a test of skill.

That's about all we can talk about now, but know that we're hard at work on the demo. In the meantime, we want to connect with you! If you haven't already, you can join our Discord or follow us on social media where we'll post updates and answer any questions that you have.


Twitter
Instagram
Facebook


Thank you for your time,
-Smithy, Hybrid Fiction Games
